subject: Post-demo: pricing/throughput calibration for ACME inference pipeline
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Taylor <evan@acme.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & sizing questions (throughput + $/1M tokens targets)

Evan — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can put together a targeted Dedicated proposal and a recommended GPU mix. Notes below are from our call + two asks at the end.

Summary of what you shared:
- Workload: multi-turn summarization + retrieval-augmented generation for customer support (avg. 550 tokens/request; 70% of calls include 2+ turns)
- Expected steady-state: 120M tokens/day (7-day average)
- Peak/day bursts: up to 480M tokens/day during releases (1–2 hour windows)
- Latency SLO: 150–250 ms p50 for short responses, up to 600 ms acceptable p95 for longer chains
- High availability: want regional redundancy in us-west with automated fallback
- Target procurement budget: $25k–$40k / month for inference (you mentioned this is the current target range)

Pricing & unit-econ framing we discussed:
- Your target $/1M tokens: ~$80–$100 would hit the higher end of your budget at scale; $120/1M pushes you over the stated range for peak usage
- Dedicated sizing ballpark: H100s give better headroom for large context and mixed workloads; A100 80GB is more cost-effective for higher concurrency if attentive to quantization

Two asks before we put together a formal Dedicated quote and perf-sims: 
1) Can you share the token distribution CSV you mentioned (avg/min/max per request + concurrency by hour) — that lets us simulate batching and pick the right pool size.
2) Confirm whether 99% of inference traffic will be for the RAG pipeline (vs. occasional multimodal/embedding-heavy jobs) — that affects whether we recommend a hybrid pool (2xH100 + 6xA100) or uniform (A100-only).

Provisional sizing (very rough):
- If traffic is 120M steady / 480M peak and we optimize batching + KV cache: 4xA100-80GB reserved (with autoscale burst to 8) could meet throughput with ~250–320 ms p95 depending on prompt shapes.
- For lower-latency and headroom on long contexts: 2xH100 + 4xA100 reserved (H100s handle longest contexts; A100s for sustained throughput).

Next steps (proposed):
- You: send token estimates and sample prompt set (CSV) — attachment stub accepted.
- Us: run a perf sim and deliver a 2-option proposal (A100-focused and hybrid H100/A100) with modeled $/1M token and monthly cost at steady + peak.
- If procurement wants, we can also provide a 60-day trial PO with usage caps for verification.

Attachments: acme_token_estimates.csv (placeholder), network_integration_notes.docx (we'll add minimal network requirements).

Thanks — cc'ing Markus and Priyom to scope benchmarks and pricing.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0114

From: Evan Taylor <evan@acme.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & sizing questions (throughput + $/1M tokens targets)

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful and matches my notes. A few clarifications below: 

- I attached the token estimate CSV (acme_token_estimates.csv) — columns: hour, requests, avg_tokens, p95_tokens, spike_factor. The 480M/day number is from last year’s holiday peak; our normal spikes are closer to ~300M but we want to plan for the higher burst.
- The RAG pipeline is ~92% of traffic; the rest are embeddings/checkpointing jobs. We can probably stage those to off-peak, so hybrid recommendation sounds reasonable.
- Budget: procurement has indicated $30k/mo target for sustained months; they are willing to stretch in Q4 for launch verification but need firm unit-econ to justify.

Procurement loop: procurement@acme.ai — can you confirm any required billing terms (PO vs invoice, net30)? Also, Evan — please include an estimate for a trial period and whether Redwood can provide a temporary commit discount for the trial window.

— Evan
Evan Taylor | Head of Platform | ACME AI Labs
Evan@acme.ai | +1-206-555-0199

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Evan Taylor <evan@acme.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & sizing questions (throughput + $/1M tokens targets)

Evan — looping in to scope perf sims. Quick technical clarifications from my side before we start modeling: 

1) Context lengths you expect to use in production (avg vs long-tail p99). You mentioned a lot of 2–4 turn threads; what’s the typical context token count for the longest 1% of requests?
2) Do you have a target p95 latency for the RAG path specifically when retrieval is included? That helps us size cache and batch windows.
3) For the trial: are you OK with a limited 30-day test that pins you to a 4-GPU reserved pool (A100 80GB) with optional burst credits for H100s if needed? We can give a temporary 20% commit credit for verification usage during the trial window.

Preliminary modeling notes (will refine after we get the CSV + sample prompts):
- Using your CSV, we can run a simulated 24-hour run and estimate tokens/sec and expected batching efficiency. If we can hit >3.5 batching factor on average, the $/1M tokens can drop ~18–25% vs raw single-request costing.
- If ACME needs <250 ms p95 at peak, hybrid with 2xH100 recommended since A100-only will likely need larger pool size and cost more overall to hit that latency.

I'll start the perf sims today; Soojin, Priyom and I will sync on the numbers and send two concrete proposals (A100-only reserved and hybrid reserved) by EOD Thursday.

— Markus
Markus Klein | Sales Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: Evan Taylor <evan@acme.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & sizing questions (throughput + $/1M tokens targets)

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We can get the sample prompt sets over by EOD Thursday. Procurement confirms PO + net30 is preferred. The 20% trial credit sounds reasonable; please include the trial terms in the proposal.

Evan
